answer: Streetlights on one circuit switch on within the same second each evening, so a claimant senses the local switch-on time and its street must agree with the municipal controller's log for that circuit. Three consecutive evenings are required, since a single lucky guess cannot repeat; a tundra datacentre cannot guess the exact second for many streets at once, an island of fake circuits fails against the public schedule, and no voyage of copied timestamps survives the sunset drift of local timers.
